title: Recording: Daytime Nighttime Suffering by Wings | 1979
content:
Replica Studio, London
Producers: Paul McCartney, Chris Thomas

Wings’ first studio session of 1979 was for the ‘Goodnight Tonight’ single b-side ‘Daytime Nighttime Suffering’.

The song came out of a band discussion in the MPL boardroom on 12 January. Paul McCartney said they needed to release a new single, and set a challenge for the group.

I remember him saying, ‘I challenge you all to go home and write your best effort, and we’ll review them all on Monday. And whoever’s written the best song is the one we record.’ I honestly don’t remember what I did, but I know I put something together and Denny put something together, and Laurence, and we all came in and one by one played what we had. And then I remember Paul saying, ‘Well, I wrote this,’ and that was ‘Daytime Nighttime Suffering’. And we all collectively went, ‘Ahh, okay. Well, let’s record that one then!’
Steve Holley, 1 July 2020
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 2: 1974-80

Recording began on 15 January 1979 at Replica Studio in the MPL basement. McCartney played an RMI electric piano, Denny Laine and Laurence Juber played electric guitars, and Steve Holley was on drums.

There weren’t too many times when Paul gave me specific things to play. There’s a little guitar lick on ‘Daytime Nighttime Suffering’ that he had me play because he wrote the song with that lick. But most of the time I was free to do my own thing.
Laurence Juber
Goldmine, 2 November 2001

Six tape reels were filled with takes before a master version was recorded, although several of the attempts ended in jam sessions.

‘Daytime Nighttime Suffering’ was completed the following day.
